summary.en: The prime minister has shared his condolences for the family and friends of the 50-year-old soldier who died on Monday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The prime minister has paid tribute to Lachlan Muddle, a special forces soldier who died in a training accident on Monday evening.

Special Air Service Regiment soldier Warrant Officer Class Two Muddle, 50, sustained fatal injuries during a parachute training exercise at the Jervis Bay Airfield on the NSW south coast, the Department of Defence has shared.

Muddle, a paratrooper and sniper with 30 years of experience in the defence force, collided with a fellow soldier about a hundred feet above the ground during a high-altitude training exercise for the Australian Defence Force's (ADF) parachute school, a senior officer confirmed.

Special Operations Commander Major General Garth Gould told reporters on Tuesday that the two men had already opened their parachutes when the collision occurred.

"Both paratroopers were highly skilled, between the two of them they had several thousand jumps to their credit," he said.

The other soldier involved sustained minor injuries and was the first to provide first aid assistance to Muddle. The incident occurred in the early evening during low light conditions.

"The death of one of our soldiers is a tragedy and deeply felt by the army family and across the broader defence community", the Department of Defence shared in a statement.

"Our highest priority is to support Warrant Officer Class Two Muddle’s family and all members involved in this tragic accident.

"Our thoughts are with them, their friends and the Regiment as they grieve his loss."

All parachute operations have been paused across Australia while initial investigations into the incident are conducted.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the accident is a tragedy and a "stark reminder" that "there are no easy days for those who defend our nation".

"Our hearts also go out to his army family and the broader defence community," Albanese said in a statement. "We are in the debt of every Australian who serves and puts themselves on the line for all of us."

Defence Minister Richard Marles also shared his condolences on Tuesday, describing Muddle as one of the ADF's "finest".

"Our thoughts are with Warrant Officer Muddle's family, as they are with his friends and his defence family," he said in a statement.

The Returned and Services League of Australia (RSL) NSW extended its "deepest condolences" to Muddle's family, friends, and colleagues.

"Training accidents are a stark reminder of the risks our servicemen and women continue to face in service to the nation, both here at home and abroad," they wrote in a statement.

The death is the first in a parachuting accident since Lance Corporal Jack Fitzgibbon, son of former federal defence minister Joel Fitzgibbon, died in March 2024 during a training incident at RAAF Base Richmond, northwest of...
body.zh: 总理向周一晚上在训练事故中丧生的特种部队士兵拉克兰·穆德尔表示敬意。 美国国防部透露，50 岁的特种空勤团二级准尉穆德尔在新南威尔士州南海岸杰维斯湾机场的一次跳伞训练演习中受了致命伤。 一名高级军官证实，在澳大利亚国防军 (ADF) 降落伞学校进行高空训练演习时，在国防军中有 30 年经验的伞兵兼狙击手马德尔在距地面约 100 英尺的地方与一名战友相撞。 特种作战司令加斯·古尔德少将周二告诉记者，碰撞发生时两人已经打开降落伞。 他说：“两名伞兵的技术都很高，他们两人的跳伞次数达到了数千次。” 另一名士兵受了轻伤，他是第一个向穆德尔提供急救的人。事件发生在傍晚时分，光线较暗。 国防部在一份声明中表示：“我们一名士兵的死亡是一场悲剧，军队家庭和整个国防界对此深感悲痛。” “我们的首要任务是支持二级准尉穆德尔的家人和所有参与这场悲惨事故的成员。 “当他们为他的去世感到悲痛时，我们的心与他们、他们的朋友和军团同在。” 澳大利亚各地的所有降落伞行动均已暂停，同时对事件进行初步调查。 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯表示，这起事故是一场悲剧，并“鲜明地提醒”“对于那些保卫我们国家的人来说，日子并不轻松”。 阿尔巴内塞在一份声明中说：“我们的心也与他的军人家属和更广泛的国防界同在。” “我们欠每一个为我们所有人服务、冒着生命危险的澳大利亚人的恩情。” 周二，国防部长理查德·马尔斯也表达了哀悼，称马德尔是澳大利亚国防军“最优秀的”之一。 他在一份声明中说：“我们与马德尔准尉的家人同在，也与他的朋友和辩护家庭同在。” 新南威尔士州澳大利亚归国与服务联盟 (RSL) 向 Muddle 的家人、朋友和同事表示“最深切的哀悼”。 他们在一份声明中写道：“训练事故清楚地提醒我们，无论是在国内还是国外，我们的男女军人在为国家服务时继续面临风险。” 这是自前联邦国防部长乔尔·菲茨吉本 (Joel Fitzgibbon) 的儿子杰克·菲茨吉本 (Jack Fitzgibbon) 准尉于 2024 年 3 月在澳大利亚西北部的里士满皇家空军基地 (RAAF Base Richmond) 的一次训练事故中丧生以来，这是第一起跳伞事故。

title.en: 'Brutal oppression': Australian government imposes new sanctions on Iranian officials
title.zh: “残酷镇压”：澳大利亚政府对伊朗官员实施新制裁

summary.en: The Australian government has imposed over 230 sanctions on Iranian individuals and entities to date.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia is imposing targeted financial penalties and travel bans on senior Iranian officials responsible for the oppression of women and girls under the regime's crackdown on society.

Seven Iranians and four entities are being sanctioned in response to Iran's "brutal" ongoing oppression of its people, in addition to the wrongful detention of foreigners, Foreign Minister Penny Wong announced on Tuesday.

Independent estimates suggest Iranian forces killed more than 30,000 people as protests erupted throughout the country in January. Iranian government figures put that number much lower.

The sanctioned officials included interior minister Eskandar Momeni, who is also deputy commander in chief of the law enforcement forces, which is responsible for the deaths of the protesters .

Ruhollah Nasab is another high-ranking official targeted by Australia's sanctions, for his role in deploying 80,000 forces to ensure mandatory hijab-wearing by Iranian women and surveil their dress in schools, universities, public spaces and online.

The sanctions will also target Iran's shadow banking system, which allows it to fund proxies such as Hamas — which Australia considers a terrorist organisation — and support its ballistic missile program.

The Albanese government has so far imposed more than 230 sanctions on Iranian individuals and entities.

The announcement on Tuesday was made alongside the United Kingdom's sanctions on Iran.

Wong said Australia will continue its work with international partners to hold the regime to account for its "egregious campaign of oppression and destabilisation".

"Australia continues to stand with the brave people of Iran against a brutal, oppressive regime," she said.

Although the sanctions target Iran's destabilising actions throughout the Middle East, they are not in direct response to the retaliatory strikes in the US-led war.

The strikes launched by the US and Israel have resulted in the effective closure of one of the world's most important oil corridors, the Strait of Hormuz, sending the price of fuel soaring globally.

body.zh: 澳大利亚正在对伊朗高级官员实施有针对性的经济处罚和旅行禁令，这些官员应对伊朗政权对社会的镇压中压迫妇女和女孩负责。 外交部长黄英贤周二宣布，除了错误拘留外国人外，七名伊朗人和四个实体正在受到制裁，以回应伊朗对其人民持续的“残酷”压迫。 独立估计显示，1 月份全国各地爆发抗议活动时，伊朗军队已造成 30,000 多人死亡。伊朗政府的数据显示这个数字要低得多。 受到制裁的官员包括内政部长埃斯坎达尔·莫梅尼(Eskandar Momeni)，他也是执法部队的副总司令，该部队对抗议者的死亡负有责任。 鲁霍拉·纳萨布 (Ruhollah Nasab) 是另一位受到澳大利亚制裁的高级官员，因为他部署了 80,000 名军队，确保伊朗妇女强制戴头巾，并在学校、大学、公共场所和网络上监控她们的着装。 制裁还将针对伊朗的影子银行系统，该系统使其能够为哈马斯（澳大利亚视为恐怖组织）等代理人提供资金，并支持其弹道导弹计划。 阿尔巴尼亚政府迄今已对伊朗个人和实体实施了230多项制裁。 周二宣布这一消息的同时，英国也对伊朗实施了制裁。 黄说，澳大利亚将继续与国际伙伴合作，追究该政权“恶劣的镇压和破坏稳定活动”的责任。 她说：“澳大利亚继续与勇敢的伊朗人民站在一起，反对残暴、压迫的政权。” 尽管制裁针对的是伊朗在整个中东地区的破坏稳定行为，但它们并不是对美国领导的战争中的报复性打击的直接回应。 美国和以色列发动的袭击导致世界上最重要的石油走廊之一霍尔木兹海峡被有效关闭，导致全球燃油价格飙升。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

summary.en: Housing and cost-of-living pressures of young Australians loom large as Labor prepares to unveil sweeping budget reforms.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Opposition's finance spokesperson has suggested gen Z Australians are increasingly worried about the long-term debt burden they may inherit, as Labor prepares to unveil a budget pitched as a mix of reform and restraint.

Speaking on ABC radio on Tuesday, Claire Chandler said younger Australians were carrying a widening set of concerns, with housing not the only pressure shaping their view of the economy.

"I think there are a lot of concerns in the minds of young Australians. Certainly, access to housing is one of them," she said.

"But I also think there's this real awareness now that government needs to be spending within its means."

Opposition treasury spokesperson Tim Wilson has intensified that criticism, accusing the government of preparing to "kneecap" the future of young Australians through its budget decisions.

The Coalition's broader resistance to anticipated tax changes in tonight's budget — including possible reforms to capital gains tax, negative gearing and taxation of trusts — appears to rest on the framing that younger Australians are increasingly concerned about fiscal expansion and the long-term consequences of government debt.

But for many young Australians navigating post-pandemic uncertainty, soaring housing costs, rising living expenses and broader global instability, immediate, not future, financial pressures remain their defining concern, polling from early 2026 suggests.

summary.en: For some men, a lack of emotional resources means profound struggle and suicidal ideation can follow breakups.

body.en:
Tim Hewson vividly remembers the moment he realised the impact of the breakdown of his long-term marriage.

"I started scrolling through my mobile phone thinking, 'Who can I reach out to? Who can I call?'" the 52-year-old told The Feed.

"I realised there wasn't a single bloke in my life that I could really open up to. That's quite a lonely experience."

"I looked in the mirror and the guy staring back at me was someone I never thought I'd become. I was in my early 40s, separated and in the fast lane to divorce. And while I was trying to work out what my life looked like, my thoughts were spiralling out of control."

One in four people who go through a relationship breakdown experience loneliness, according to a 2024 Relationships Australia report, which surveyed about 3,000 people.

But men who experienced a breakup are 82 per cent more likely to report suicidal ideation relative to men without a recent breakup experience, according to a long-term Australian study published in the Journal of Affective Disorders last year that surveyed over 16,000 men and analysed their experiences a year after separation.

One of the authors, Michael Wilson, a research fellow with the Movember Institute, told The Feed some of these negative mental health outcomes were reported by men who had not previously experienced poor mental health.

"Separated men relative to their married counterparts are at up to five times greater risk of suicide," Wilson told The Feed.

While Tim didn't experience suicidal ideation, he said the breakup took a major toll on his mental health.

"Relationship breakdowns are challenging enough, but breaking up families can be even harder — you're now alone," Tim said.

"With isolation and loneliness comes anxiety, depression, and that can lead to a sense of helplessness and hopelessness."

Wilson said many men rely heavily on their partner as their main source of emotional support, which can make breakups particularly difficult.

"The one person through which you typically cope with really intense, stressful experiences is the one person that you now don't necessarily have access to," he said.

But how men navigate distress — shaped by ideas of masculinity and a lack of social and emotional support — may also explain why many men struggle so profoundly after breakups.

For men, romantic relationships can often be the only avenue where vulnerability and emotions feel safe, according to Wilson.

"A lot of guys [in the research] talk about how their partner is the only one that truly knows them," Wilson said.
